body.objective: Add a deterministic out-of-core execution and cache layer for large exact expression DAGs, sparse matrices, tensor contractions and modular batches. The programme has already suffered OOMs, and the new generic kernels will not be adopted broadly if every resident must materialize hundred-thousand-term q2/q3 expressions or large certificate closures in memory. This is mathematical execution infrastructure: cached objects must preserve coefficient domain, assumptions, truncation order, basis and proof provenance so Conflux can reuse structure without confusing a cached scout with a verified theorem. The first consumers are sf:program/work/nonlinear-cyclic-deformation-class-completeness, sf:program/work/observer-higher-jet-invariant-action-module-classification and sf:program/work/quantum-parameterized-five-form-factor-independent-audit.
body.stop_condition: Provide canonical content hashes for typed exact objects; chunked immutable storage for sparse matrices, polynomials, tensors and expression DAGs; deterministic streaming map/reduce for addition, multiplication, substitution, contraction and modular elimination; checkpoint/restart with provenance-safe invalidation; reference-counted or reachability-based cache GC; disk, memory, CPU and wall-time budgets; and atomic publication of completed objects only. Partial chunks must remain visibly INCOMPLETE and unusable as claims. Add cost estimates and a dry-run plan so Conflux can choose an equivalent lower-peak evaluation order. Demonstrate byte-identical cold and warm results on one >100,000-term interaction carrier, one sparse exact solve and one tensor contraction; force an OOM-budget refusal and resume from the last valid checkpoint; mutate one upstream basis/assumption and prove only dependent chunks invalidate. Record peak RSS, disk use, cache hits, elapsed time and verification rail in the receipt.
body.forbid: no pickle or process-specific hash as a scientific identifier; no cache hit across coefficient domains, assumptions, bases or truncation orders; no partial checkpoint treated as a completed object; no nondeterministic parallel reduction that changes exact serialization; no unbounded cache growth; no deletion of another live worker's referenced chunks; no numeric compression of exact coefficients; no performance result without a cold reference and correctness replay
notes: This complements the Science Forge process resource governor: the governor enforces limits, while this layer lets exact algebra make progress within them and resume safely.
A first slice can target expression DAGs plus modular sparse batches, then generalize the same object protocol to tensors and polynomial ideals.
